gaps.sentence: Unemployment has ___ sharply since the spring.
gaps.explanation: 'Has risen' — rise does not take an object.

gaps.sentence: I'm exhausted — I need to ___ down and rest.
gaps.hint: to recline — no object; forms: lie, lay, lain
gaps.explanation: 'Lie' (lie, lay, lain) means to recline and takes no object; 'lay' (lay, laid, laid) means to put something down and takes an object.

gaps.sentence: There is little ___ that the plan will be approved.
gaps.hint: pattern: little ___ that something will happen
gaps.explanation: 'Possibility that ...' is the standard pattern; 'opportunity' means a situation that lets you do something.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ to rain later, so take a coat.
gaps.explanation: 'It's likely to rain' — probable; 'alike' means similar.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.
'Especially' means in particular or above all; 'specially' means for one particular purpose.

gaps.sentence: After twenty years of service, she is one of our most ___ employees.
gaps.explanation: 'A valued member/employee' is someone the organisation appreciates; 'valuable' stresses monetary or practical worth.

gaps.sentence: He is very ___ to criticism and takes it personally.
gaps.hint: easily affected or hurt; pattern: ___ to
gaps.explanation: 'Sensitive to something' means easily affected or upset by it; 'sensible' means showing good judgement.
